title: Trademark Objection
description: Aanoor Global can help you draft a trademark objection reply that addresses the examiner's concerns and increases the chances of your TM application being approved. Our objection reply service includes various stages to file the response.

template.value: When you apply to register a trademark, the trademark examiner may raise an objection to a trademark application at the initial stage of the registration process. This can happen for a number of reasons, such as if the trademark is too similar to another registered trademark, or if it is descriptive of the goods or services it is used for. If you have received an objection to your trademark application, contact Aanoor Global today to learn more about our objection reply service. We can help you get your application approved and protect your brand.

value: Object drafting
Reply filing
MIS-R report
Brand reply consultation

value.title: Objection of Application
value: The trademark examiner is responsible for raising objections to trademark applications. They are appointed by the trademark registry and are responsible for examining trademark applications to ensure that they meet the requirements for registration.

value.title: Examination Report
value: If your trademark application is objected to, you will receive an examination report that explains the reasons for the objection. You will have 30 days to file a reply to the objection.

value.title: Response to Objection
value: Your reply to the objection should address the concerns raised by the trademark examiner. You may need to provide evidence to support your arguments, such as a copy of a prior registration for a similar trademark or a survey of consumers.

value.title: Response to TM reply
value: If the trademark examiner is satisfied with your reply, they will approve your application and it will be published in the trademark journal. If the trademark examiner is not satisfied with your reply, they will reject your application.

template.id: A trademark can be objected to for a variety of reasons
template.header: A trademark can be objected to for a variety of reasons
value: It is too similar to another registered trademark.
It is descriptive of the goods or services it is used for.
It is a prohibited name, such as a swear word or a name that is likely to confuse consumers.
It is deceptive or misleading
It is detrimental to the public interest.

template.desc: It is important to note that trademark objections are common and do not necessarily mean that your application will be rejected. If you receive an objection, it is important to carefully review the examination report and file a strong reply. With careful preparation, you can overcome most trademark objections and register your trademark. Here is a more detailed explanation of the services included in our trademark objection reply service:

value.title: Object drafting
value: Our trademark attorneys have extensive experience drafting trademark objection replies. They will carefully review the examiner's objections and draft a reply that addresses each one in a clear and concise manner.

value.title: MIS-R report
value: We will obtain a MIS-R report, which is a search report that lists all of the registered trademarks that are similar to yours. This report will help us to craft a stronger objection reply.

value.title: Brand Objection consultation
value: We will consult with you throughout the objection reply process to ensure that your interests are protected. We will answer any questions you have and make sure that you are satisfied with the outcome of the process.

value.title: Reply filing
value: We will file your reply with the trademark office on your behalf. We will also keep you updated on the status of your application and let you know when your reply has been accepted.

value.title: Proceed for TM Objection

template.desc: The Trademark Act, 1999 governs trademark hearings in India. The Act provides for a two-stage TM hearing process in Chennai:

value.title: Preliminary hearing
value: The preliminary hearing is held to determine whether there are any prima facie grounds for the trademark hearing. If the Registrar finds that there are prima facie grounds, the trademark hearing will proceed to the next stage.

value.title: Final hearing
value: The final hearing is held to resolve the dispute between the trademark owners. The Registrar will consider all of the evidence presented by the parties and will make a decision on the merits of the case.The tm hearing process can be complex and time-consuming. It is important to have an experienced trademark attorney to represent you at a trademark hearing. An experienced trademark attorney will be able to help you prepare your case and present your arguments to the Registrar.
Applicant or registrant name and address
Opposite party name and address
The trademark registration number (if applicable)
A brief summary of the dispute

desc: Here are the steps involved in tm hearing:

value: We will file Form TM-H with the given information on behalf of applicant for registration of the trademark with the Trademark Registry.

value.title: Filing of Opposition
value: If an opposition is filed against the trademark application, the Trademark Registry will schedule a preliminary hearing to determine whether there are any prima facie grounds for the trademark hearing.

value.title: Prima facie grounds
value: If the Registrar finds that there are prima facie grounds for the trademark hearing, the trademark hearing will proceed to the next stage.

value.title: Filing of Responses
value: The trademark applicant and the opponent will file written submissions and evidence in support of their respective cases.

value.title: Final Hearing
value: The Registrar will hold a final hearing to resolve the dispute between the trademark owners. The Registrar will make a decision on the merits of the case and issue a ruling.

template.value: The Patents Act, 1970 governs patent registration in India. The Act defines a patent as an exclusive right granted by the Government of India to the inventor for a limited period of time to prevent others from making, using, selling, or importing the invention without the consent of the inventor.

template.id: Criteria for filing a Patent right registration
template.header: Criteria for filing a Patent right registration

value.title: Novelty:
value: The invention must be new and not previously known to the public in India or anywhere else in the world.

value.title: Non-obviousness:
value: The invention must involve an inventive step, meaning that it must be something that would not have been obvious to a person skilled in the art at the time of the invention.

value.title: Industrial applicability:
value: The invention must be capable of industrial application, meaning that it must be capable of being used in a commercial or industrial setting.

template.id: Benefits of Patent Registration in Chennai
template.header: Benefits of Patent Registration in Chennai

value.title: Sell or transfer patent rights:
value: Patent registration gives you the exclusive right to make, use, sell, or import your invention for a period of 20 years. This means that you can sell or transfer your patent rights to another party, which can be a great way to raise capital or expand your business.

value.title: Secure your invention:
value: Patent registration is one of the strongest forms of intellectual property protection available. It gives you the legal right to prevent from others making, using, selling, or importing your invention without your consent. This can help you to protect your investment in research and development and to maintain a competitive advantage in the marketplace.

value.title: Get royalty by patent licensing:
value: You can also license your patent to another party, which means that they can use your invention in exchange for paying you a royalty. This can be a great way to generate passive income from your invention.

value.title: Make use of your invention:
value: Patent registration does not just prevent others from using your invention. It also gives you the right to use your invention yourself. This means that you can bring your invention to market and start generating profits.

value.title: Stop others from using your invention without permission:
value: Patent registration gives you the legal right to stop others from using your invention without your permission. This can be a powerful tool for protecting your intellectual property and for enforcing your rights.

value.subHeading: Here are some additional details about the patent registration services:

steps.heading: Application for Patent
steps.desc: The first step in the design patent registration process is to file a patent application with the Indian Patent Office. The application must include a description of the invention, drawings if necessary, and claims that define the scope of the invention.

steps.heading: Identification of Novelty
steps.desc: The patent office will then conduct a search of prior art to determine whether the invention is novel and inventive. If the invention is found to be novel and inventive, it will be published for public inspection.

steps.heading: Opposition to Patent
steps.desc: Any person who believes that the invention is not novel or inventive can file an opposition to the patent application. The patent office will then decide whether to grant the patent.

steps.heading: Approval of Patent
steps.desc: If the Indian patent register is granted, the inventor will have the exclusive right to make, use, sell, or import the invention for a period of 20 years.
